items.name: standalone
items.title: Standalone
items.description: Whether the app runs from the home screen, safe to read during a server render.

items.name: pull-refresh
items.title: Pull to refresh
items.description: WhatsApp-style pull to refresh: the page stays put and a circle follows the finger. Installed apps only by default.

items.name: tab-bar
items.title: Tab bar
items.description: A floating bottom bar under the thumb with a gliding active pill. Works with any router's links.

items.name: install
items.title: Install card
items.description: Add to home screen in whatever form the browser supports: Chromium's prompt, iOS's two taps, or out of an in-app browser.
items.docs: Call captureInstallPrompt() from @/lib/install in your client entry, before React mounts: Chromium fires beforeinstallprompt once and early.

items.name: boot
items.title: Boot screen
items.description: The logo stays up from the splash until the first real screen has rendered, one colour end to end, so opening the app never flashes a blank screen.
items.docs:
1. index.html, after #root:
, styled #boot { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 2147483647; display: grid; place-items: center; background: %BOOT_BG%; transition: opacity 0.2s } #boot.out { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none } #boot svg { width: min(35vmin, 280px); aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 22.27%; overflow: hidden }, plus html { background: %BOOT_BG% } and theme-color %BOOT_BG%. 2. vite.config.ts: bootScreen({ background, logo }) from ./vite-boot-screen, background from pwa-assets.config (the app-assets item). 3. Client entry, before React mounts: startBoot(), and bootReady() on the first render, e.g. const stop = router.subscribe("onRendered", () => { stop(); bootReady(); }). 4. A screen that is only a loading placeholder calls useBootHold(isLoading).

items.name: app-assets
items.title: Icons and splash screens
items.description: Icons, favicon, maskable icon and every Apple splash screen from one logo and one background colour, the same colour the boot screen and manifest use.
items.docs: Set background (the app's page colour as hex) and logo in pwa-assets.config.ts, put <!-- pwa-assets:start --> and <!-- pwa-assets:end --> in index.html's head, then run bun scripts/generate-assets.ts after every logo change. Give the manifest the same background as background_color and theme_color.
